findings.title: Start the server event watcher before indexing
findings.body: The server watcher is now started only after `s.search.init`, which can take a long time. `WatchWriteEvents` establishes its polling cursor from the latest resource version when it starts, so writes committed during index construction are already behind that cursor and will never be emitted. A client watching from a resource version before startup can therefore miss those changes. Start the watcher before the potentially slow index build, or replay events from a durable cursor.

findings.title: Serialize builds for the same index key
findings.body: Removing the build-wide lock allows concurrent `BuildIndex` calls for the same key: callers can both observe a missing index in `getOrCreateIndex` before either build caches its result, and there is no per-key build coordination. For file-backed indexes, both builds can concurrently open/create the same Bleve directory; for memory-backed indexes, one build can overwrite the other's cached index while callers still hold the other instance. This can cause build failures or leave writes applied to an index that is no longer served. Preserve parallel builds for different keys while serializing builds per key.

findings.title: Clean up resources when initialization fails
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now runs `s.Init` and returns `nil` on error without canceling `s.ctx` or stopping the lifecycle backend. If failure occurs after `s.search.init` starts its background event watcher—for example, if the subsequent `initWatcher` call fails—the constructor loses the server handle while the watcher and initialized backend can remain running. Clean up initialized resources before returning the error.
